items.title: Itô SDE data and strong solution
items.statement: On a finite usual filtered Brownian space, specify the vector Itô SDE, coefficient, initial-value, integrability and strong-solution conventions for finite dimensions d and m.
items.strategy: Use finite-horizon restrictions of the published Brownian and stochastic-integral constructions; explicitly cap energy localizers at T and paste their compatible finite-energy integrals. State coefficient, initial-value and solution conventions.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is inherited from the declared stochastic-integral interface.

references.title: Ramon van Handel, Stochastic Calculus, Filtering, and Stochastic Control: Lecture Notes, Chapter 5.1
A.W. van der Vaart, Martingales, Diffusions and Financial Mathematics (preliminary notes), Section 7.1

items.title: Well-definedness and estimates for the Lipschitz SDE map
items.statement: For square-integrable continuous adapted inputs, the Picard map for the finite-dimensional Itô SDE is well-defined, maps into the same path-space class, and satisfies explicit growth, difference and first-iterate estimates.
items.strategy: Prove predictability and finite energy from the linear-growth bound, then use Cauchy–Schwarz for the drift, coordinatewise Itô isometry and Doob bounds for the matrix integral, and the Frobenius norm for the finite coordinate sums.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is inherited from the declared Itô-integral and martingale interfaces.

references.title: Ramon van Handel, Stochastic Calculus, Filtering, and Stochastic Control: Lecture Notes, Chapter 5.1

items.title: A Lipschitz SDE solution has a finite path-sup second moment
items.statement: Any adapted continuous solution under the local strong-solution integrability convention has finite E sup |X_t|^2 under the global linear-growth bound, proved by stopping, Itô's formula, Gronwall and Fatou.
items.strategy: Stop a locally integrable solution at increasing radii; apply Itô to 1+|X|^2, take expectations after finite-energy localization, prove the stopped Gronwall bound, remove the stop with Fatou, and then use the SDE integral equation, Itô maximal estimates and linear growth to obtain E sup |X|^2 < infinity.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is inherited from the declared Itô formula and stochastic-integral interfaces.

items.title: Global strong well-posedness for Lipschitz Itô SDEs
items.statement: For jointly Borel coefficients with uniform global state Lipschitz and linear-growth bounds and an independent square-integrable F_0 initial value, there is an adapted continuous strong solution on every finite horizon; it is pathwise unique up to indistinguishability and has a finite E sup |X_t|^2 bound.
items.strategy: Construct the fixed point by Picard iteration, derive factorial bounds for successive path-sup differences, pass the limit through the drift and diffusion integrals, then prove the path-sup bound and uniqueness by integral Gronwall estimates.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is inherited from the declared stochastic-integral and martingale interfaces.

items.title: Finite-horizon moments for Lipschitz Itô SDEs
items.statement: For every real p >= 2 and X_0 in L^p, the unique solution under the same global Lipschitz and linear-growth hypotheses satisfies sup_{t <= T} E|X_t|^p <= C(1 + E|X_0|^p); all finite p moments follow when X_0 has all finite p moments.
items.strategy: Apply the multidimensional Itô formula to V(x)=(1+|x|^2)^(p/2), stop at the first exit from a radius, bound its generator by C_p V, take expectations after the stopped martingale has finite energy, apply integral Gronwall, and remove the stop by Fatou.

items.title: A scalar Ornstein–Uhlenbeck SDE satisfies the strong well-posedness hypotheses
items.statement: For b(t,x)=-theta x with theta >= 0 and sigma(t,x)=sigma_0 != 0, verify the assumptions of the strong Itô SDE theorem for any F_0-measurable X_0 in L^2 independent of future Brownian increments.
items.strategy: Check joint Borel measurability, the uniform global Lipschitz and linear-growth estimates, the initial-data hypotheses and the scalar nondegenerate constant diffusion; then apply the local strong well-posedness theorem.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is inherited from the strong solution theorem.

items.title: A deterministic initial law is singular although the SDE is well-posed
items.statement: For b=0, sigma=1 and X_0=0, all global Lipschitz and linear-growth hypotheses hold and the SDE is strongly well-posed, while the initial law is a point mass and has no Lebesgue density at t=0.
items.strategy: Verify the scalar coefficient and initial-value assumptions, apply the strong well-posedness theorem, and evaluate the initial law on the Lebesgue-null singleton {0}.
items.axiom_base: Full AC is inherited from the strong solution theorem.
